result: Experiment 1 demonstrated that sensory preconditioned fear occurs with both few (8) and many (32) sound-light pairings, with stronger fear responses observed after 32 pairings compared to 8 pairings. The interaction between number of pairings and stimulus relation confirmed that fear responses require formation of both sound-light and light-shock memories rather than generalization.
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly affirmed these findings. Reviewer 1 stated 'Experiment 1 demonstrated the sensory preconditioned fear with few (8) or many (32) sound-light pairings.' Reviewer 3 confirmed 'sensory preconditioning was successful with either 8 or 32 stimulus-stimulus pairings.' No concerns were raised about these behavioral results.

result: Experiments 2A and 2B showed that PRh NMDA receptor activity during stage 2 conditioning is required for sensory preconditioning after few (8) but not many (32) sound-light pairings. This differential requirement indicates that rats form a mediated sound-shock memory during conditioning after few pairings, but use a chaining mechanism after many pairings.
evaluation: Reviewers unanimously supported these findings. Reviewer 1 noted 'Experiments 2A and 2B showed the role of PRh NMDA receptors during conditioning for online integration, revealing that this contribution is present only after few sound-light pairings, not after many.' Reviewer 2 stated the results 'find unambiguous results that the extent of training during the preconditioning stage impacts the involvement of PRh during the first-order conditioning.' Reviewer 3 confirmed 'Perirhinal cortex NMDA receptor blockade during stimulus-outcome learning impaired preconditioning following 8 but not 32 pairings.'

result: Experiments 3A and 3B demonstrated that PRh-BLA communication during stage 2 conditioning is required for sensory preconditioning after few (8) but not many (32) sound-light pairings. Contralateral disconnection impaired fear to the preconditioned sound only in the 8-pairing condition, supporting the mediated learning mechanism for few pairings.
evaluation: All reviewers affirmed these findings without reservation. Reviewer 1 stated 'Experiments 3A and 3B showed the contribution of PRh-BLA communication to online integration, again only after few but not after many.' Reviewer 2 noted this 'confirms their previous findings in 2019 of connectivity between these regions for the short duration training, while they observe here for the first time that this is not the case for extended training.' Reviewer 3 confirmed 'Perirhinal-basolateral amygdala had nearly identical effects with the same interpretation.'

result: Experiments 4A and 4B showed that PRh-BLA communication at test is required for sensory preconditioning after many (32) but not few (8) sound-light pairings. Contralateral disconnection prior to testing impaired fear to the preconditioned sound only in the 32-pairing condition, supporting the chaining mechanism for many pairings.
evaluation: Reviewers unanimously supported these findings as a key contribution. Reviewer 1 stated 'Contrary to Experiments 3A and 3B, Experiments 4A and 4B showed the contribution of PRh-BLA communication to integration at test only after many but not few sound-light pairings.' Reviewer 2 noted 'they show that with extended training, communication between BLA and the PRh is required at the final test of the preconditioned stimulus, but not for the short duration training.' Reviewer 3 confirmed 'Disconnection prior to the probe test, when chaining might occur, had different effects: it impaired the expression of preconditioned fear in rats that received 32, but not 8, pairings.'

result: The study's primary conclusion is that the number of sound-light pairings determines how/when memory integration occurs (online during stage 2 vs. at test in stage 3), but regardless of timing, integration requires PRh-BLA communication. Event familiarity determines the mechanism but not the circuitry involved.
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly endorsed this overarching conclusion. Reviewer 2 stated 'The results are clear and extremely consistent across experiments within this paper as well as with earlier work' and noted the work 'address an important and highly debated question in the field regarding the neural and psychological mechanisms underlying sensory preconditioning.' Reviewer 3 emphasized 'the authors were successful in describing the behavioral and neurobiological mechanisms of mediated learning versus chaining in sensory preconditioning' and called the study 'highly impactful and significant.'

result: The study builds on Wong et al. 2019, which established that PRh is involved in online integration during sensory preconditioning, showing that the light activates a PRh-dependent memory of the sound during stage 2 conditioning, resulting in both direct light-shock and mediated sound-shock memories.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this background as established. Reviewer 2 stated 'This manuscript builds on the authors' earlier work, most recently Wong et al. 2019, in which they showed the importance of the perirhinal cortex (PRh) during the first-order conditioning stage of sensory preconditioning.' Reviewer 1 noted this is 'an important follow-up to their prior work - Wong et al. (2019).' No concerns were raised about these foundational claims.

result: The authors propose that increasing sound-light pairings allows rats to learn about the temporal order of stimuli, shifting from a bidirectional to unidirectional associative structure. This hypothesis explains why many pairings undermine mediated learning during conditioning but strengthen chaining at test.
evaluation: Reviewers implicitly accepted this mechanistic interpretation as reasonable. Reviewer 2 noted the discussion 'effectively comparing the current research with the prior work and offering insightful interpretations' and Reviewer 3 stated 'The discussion leaves open questions that are very much worth exploring.' The hypothesis is supported by citations to prior research on order learning in sensory preconditioning, and no reviewer challenged this interpretation.

result: The authors propose that PRh-BLA communication serves different functions during mediated learning: PRh-to-BLA communication supports acquisition of the mediated sound-shock association, while BLA-to-PRh communication supports consolidation. They further hypothesize that PRh-to-CeA pathways may mediate expression of fear responses at test.
evaluation: Reviewers treated these mechanistic hypotheses as valuable contributions to future research. Reviewer 3 specifically praised this aspect: 'The discussion leaves open questions that are very much worth exploring. For example - why did perirhinal-amygdala disconnection prior to the probe have no effect in the 8-pairing group, when bilateral perirhinal inactivation did (in Wong et al, 2019)? The authors propose that perirhinal cortex outputs bypass the amygdala during the probe test, which is an excellent hypothesis to test.' This indicates reviewer acceptance of the proposed mechanisms as plausible and testable.

result: The methods section describes experimental subjects (Long-Evans rats), housing conditions, surgical procedures for cannula implantation and lesions, drug preparation and infusion protocols, behavioral apparatus, freezing measurement procedures, and statistical power analysis.
evaluation: All reviewers affirmed the methodological rigor. Reviewer 1 stated 'Throughout the manuscript, the methods and results are clearly organized and described, and the use of statistics is solid.' Reviewer 3 emphasized 'Careful, rigorous experimental design and statistics.' Reviewer 2 noted 'The experiments here are thorough, well-conceived' and praised 'the high quality of writing.' No methodological concerns were raised.
